# 1 Enoch Chapter 102 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 102:1 — 'affrighted' vs. 'struck with fear'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "will-ye-not-be-affrighted-and-afraid?" | 'Affrighted' = archaic; double synonym |
| LOGOS | "will you not be struck with fear and trembling?" | Formal; more natural |
| PNEUMA | "won't you shudder with fear?" | Single vivid verb |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Affrighted' (EMET) is archaic. PNEUMA's 'shudder' is vivid but singular where the Ge'ez has a doubled expression. 'Struck with fear and trembling' preserves the intensification.

---

## 102:4 — Address to the dead righteous

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Fear-ye-not, ye-souls-of-the-righteous" | Literal; 'ye souls' is specific |
| LOGOS | "Fear not, you souls of the righteous" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "Don't be afraid, you souls of the righteous" | Natural; 'Don't be afraid' for 'Fear not' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS 'Fear not.' The imperative 'Fear not' (al-tifhadu) is a biblical formula (Genesis 15:1; Isaiah 41:10) that should retain its formulaic resonance. PNEUMA's natural register is appropriate but loses the formula.

---

## 102:5 — Consolation: 'body fared not according to goodness'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "your-body-fared-not-according-to-your-goodness" | Literal; 'fared not' is evocative |
| LOGOS | "your body did not receive what your goodness deserved" | Formal; clarifies the meaning |
| PNEUMA | "your body in this life didn't get what your goodness deserved" | Adds 'in this life' |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Did not receive what your goodness deserved' is the clearest formal equivalent. 'In this life' (PNEUMA) adds words not in the Ge'ez, though the meaning is implicit.

---

## 102:6–7 — Sinners' taunt

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "As-we-die, so-die-the-righteous, and-what-benefit-do-they-reap for-their-deeds?" | Literal; preserves the force |
| LOGOS | "Just as we die, so do the righteous die; and what benefit do they reap from their deeds?" | Formal |
| PNEUMA | "They die just like us. So what did being righteous get them?" | Colloquial; rhetorically effective |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The formal rendering of the taunt preserves its precise logic. PNEUMA's colloquial version is effective but the taunt in the Ge'ez is carefully constructed — its precision matters.

---

## 102:11 — Heavenly tablets

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I-know-this-mystery-and-have-read-the-heavenly-tablets" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "I know this mystery — I have read the heavenly tablets" | Formal; dash for clarity |
| PNEUMA | "I know the mystery. I have read the heavenly tablets." | Two sentences; emphatic pause |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS with dash. The dash preserves the appositive relationship: the mystery is identified as what follows. PNEUMA's period creates a stronger pause but the relationship is slightly less clear.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 5**
